title: United 93
events_chronological: Four young men pray in a hotel room and again in a departure lounge before boarding their flight.
A regional air traffic centre notices that one aircraft has stopped answering and hears a hijacker's voice on the frequency.
The national traffic operations centre begins tracking the aircraft that has gone silent.
The first aircraft strikes the north tower, and the controllers watch it on a television without believing it.
The passengers of the fourth aircraft board and sit through a long delay on the tarmac.
The military north-east sector is ordered to scramble fighters and cannot be told where to send them.
The second aircraft strikes the south tower on live television.
The national centre orders every aircraft in the country to land at once.
The third aircraft strikes the defence headquarters outside the capital.
The hijackers on the fourth aircraft kill the pilots, take the cockpit and turn the aircraft back east.
Passengers reach families and answering machines from the seat telephones and learn what has happened elsewhere.
The passengers agree among themselves that the aircraft will not be allowed to arrive wherever it is aimed.
Fighters are finally launched, unarmed, with no clear authority to shoot anything down.
The passengers rush the cabin behind a drinks trolley and fight their way towards the cockpit.
The hijacker at the controls rolls the aircraft and puts it into a dive.
The aircraft goes into a field.
syuzhet_notes: The film runs at close to the speed of the morning it depicts, cutting between the cabin, three civilian control rooms and a military sector. Nothing is a flashback and nothing is anticipated.
fabula_notes: The chronology is the published timeline of a single morning. Where two rooms are acting in the same minute, either ranking would do.
